normalized.result: Yes, saving a recognizable fallback is much better than refusing. When the page details couldn't be collected, the link was still saved showing the domain and full URL, with a clear explanation of why it looks bare, plus the ability to fill in the title and description myself and a retry option to try fetching again. That way I don't lose a link just because the app couldn't read the page — I can still keep it and make it useful. That's exactly how I'd want it to handle that case. Happy with it.
